historical_timeline.summary: Born Arjumand Banu Begum in Agra.
Marries Prince Khurram and receives the title Mumtaz Mahal.
Thirteen children born; six die in infancy or early childhood; she travels with the court on campaign.
Her thirteenth child, a daughter, is born.
The court is at Burhanpur in the Deccan during a famine.
Dies at Burhanpur in childbirth with her fourteenth child, a daughter, after a long labor; the cause is given later as postpartum hemorrhage.
Her body is moved from Burhanpur to Agra; the Taj Mahal is built as her tomb.

claims.statement: She was born Arjumand Banu Begum in Agra in April 1593; an encyclopedia, citing a seventeenth-century court history, gives 27 April 1593.
claims.clinical_interpretation: No Hijri birth date was found in the sources read.

claims.statement: Her father, Abu'l-Hasan Asaf Khan, was a Persian noble; his sister was the Empress Nur Jahan, wife of the emperor Jahangir. Her mother's family came from Qazvin in Persia.

She was betrothed to Prince Khurram, later the emperor Shah Jahan, in 1607, and married him on 10 May 1612; he gave her the title Mumtaz Mahal, rendered as 'Chosen One of the Palace' or 'the Exalted One of the Palace'.
Despite her frequent pregnancies, she travelled with her husband's entourage on his military campaigns.

Her first thirteen children were born between 1613 and 1630: Hur-ul-Nisa (1613), Jahanara (1614), Dara Shikoh (1615), Shah Shuja (1616), Roshanara (1617), Aurangzeb (1618), Izad Bakhsh (1619), Surayya Banu (1621), a son who died soon after birth (1622), Murad Bakhsh (1624), Lutf Allah (1626), Daulat Afza (1628), and Husn Ara (1630).
claims.clinical_interpretation: Thirteen births before 1631 in the encyclopedia's table; the state tourism page omits the son who died in 1622 (CLM-0012).

claims.statement: Six of her children died in infancy or early childhood before 1631: Hur-ul-Nisa at three and Surayya Banu at seven, both of smallpox; Izad Bakhsh in infancy; a son soon after birth in 1622; Lutf Allah at about eighteen months; and Daulat Afza in infancy.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Causes are given only for the two deaths from smallpox.

claims.statement: Her thirteenth child, Husn Ara, was born on 23 April 1630.

In the year 1040 AH (from August 1630) the emperor was in the Deccan with the court at Burhanpur, during a severe famine in the Deccan and Gujarat, when he ordered soup kitchens and weekly alms for as long as he remained at Burhanpur.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Her presence with the court at Burhanpur is documented by her death there (CLM-0010).

source_links.locator: Badshah-nama, fourth year of the reign

claims.statement: The court chronicler Abdul Hamid Lahori recorded that on 17 Zi-l ka'da 1040 AH she died, in the fortieth year of her age, to the great grief of her husband, having borne him eight sons and six daughters; the translators note that she died in childbirth. The date corresponds to 17 June 1631 in the Gregorian calendar, at Burhanpur, giving birth to a daughter, Gauhar Ara.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The fortieth year is counted in lunar (Hijri) years; by the Gregorian calendar she was 38.

source_links.locator: Badshah-nama, death of the Queen 'Aliya Begam

claims.statement: Later accounts state that she died after a prolonged labor of about 30 hours with her fourteenth child.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Reported by an encyclopedia citing a 2014 case report and a seventeenth-century court history; the primary text was not read.

claims.statement: The state tourism page for the Taj Mahal calls Gauhar Ara her thirteenth child and lists thirteen children, while the court chronicle counts fourteen (eight sons and six daughters).
claims.clinical_interpretation: The count of fourteen is preferred; the thirteen-child list omits the son who died soon after birth in 1622.

claims.statement: Her death is attributed to postpartum hemorrhage.
claims.clinical_interpretation: A retrospective medical reading of a death in childbirth after a long labor; no contemporary description of bleeding was read.

claims.statement: Her fourteenth child, Gauhar Ara, was born on 17 June 1631, about fourteen months after Husn Ara.
claims.clinical_interpretation: If the last pregnancy went to term, it began about five months after the previous birth.

claims.statement: She was first buried at Burhanpur in the walled Zainabad garden on the Tapti River; her body was moved to Agra in December 1631, and the Taj Mahal was built as her tomb over more than twenty years.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: High-risk prenatal care for a 37-year-old woman in her fourteenth pregnancy, conceived about five and a half months after her last birth, following ACOG Obstetric Care Consensus No. 11 (pregnancy at 35 or older), ACOG Practice Bulletin 183 and the WHO 2012 and 2017 recommendations on postpartum hemorrhage, and the WOMAN trial: dating by ultrasound when the last period is unknown, aneuploidy screening offered (cell-free DNA and nuchal translucency), blood group and antibodies, iron deficiency anemia with a hemoglobinopathy screen, oral then intravenous iron and anemia corrected before delivery, early and routine screening for gestational diabetes, blood pressure and low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia risk (USPSTF 2021), placental location and the low risk of placenta accreta without a uterine scar, asymptomatic bacteriuria and cystitis in pregnancy, travel in pregnancy, and a postpartum hemorrhage risk assessment and plan (delivery in a hospital with a blood bank and surgical capability, active management of the third stage with oxytocin, quantitative blood loss, and tranexamic acid within 3 hours of birth if hemorrhage occurs), with counseling, in her own terms, about contraception and the interval before any future pregnancy. The episode ends at 34 weeks, before delivery.

hpi.narrative: Mumtaz Mahal returns at 17 weeks 2 days. The cell-free DNA result came back low risk. She has taken ferrous sulfate every other morning for four weeks but has missed about half the doses because of nausea and constipation, and she is still tired and breathless on the stairs. She takes aspirin 81 mg at bedtime without bruising or bleeding, and folic acid. She has no headache, visual change, abdominal pain, bleeding, or urinary symptoms, and has begun to feel the baby move. She saw Dr. Montgomery-Rahimi of maternal-fetal medicine this morning.

referral.question: Fourteenth pregnancy at 37, at 13 weeks 2 days by today's scan, conceived about five and a half months after her last birth, with iron deficiency anemia. referral.pertinent_history: Mumtaz Mahal is a 37-year-old woman, gravida 14 para 13, with thirteen previous vaginal births and no cesarean or other uterine surgery; seven of her children are living. Her last baby was born nine months ago; she breastfed for five months and her periods had not returned, so today's scan is used for dating: single live intrauterine pregnancy, crown-rump length 72 mm (13 weeks 2 days), nuchal translucency 1.7 mm. She is tired and breathless on stairs. Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, MCV 76 fL, ferritin 9 ng/mL, platelets 245; hemoglobin electrophoresis sent. Hemoglobin A1c 5.4 percent (early screen: South Asian heritage and BMI 23.8). Blood pressure 104/64 mmHg. Height 157 cm, weight 58.6 kg. She starts ferrous sulfate every other day, aspirin 81 mg at bedtime (age 35 or older and a previous adverse pregnancy outcome), and folic acid today, and chose cell-free DNA screening, drawn today. She had the influenza vaccine today. EPDS 8. She travels often with her family for long periods. No medical history, medicines, or allergies otherwise
questions: What surveillance does this pregnancy need, given her age, grand multiparity, and the short interval since her last birth?
How should her iron deficiency anemia be treated, and when should we move to intravenous iron?
How should the placenta be assessed for previa and accreta after thirteen births?
When and where should she give birth, and should labor be induced?
What should the postpartum hemorrhage prevention and treatment plan include?

consultant_note.history: Mumtaz Mahal is seen at the request of Dr. Qureshi-Lindholm at 17 weeks 2 days. She has had thirteen vaginal births, all by her account at or near term, with labors that were often short, and no cesarean, uterine surgery, or blood transfusion; she does not know of heavy bleeding after any birth. One baby died soon after birth, and five other children died in infancy or early childhood. This pregnancy began about five and a half months after her last birth. She has taken about half of her oral iron doses because of nausea and constipation and remains tired. She has no bleeding, pain, or urinary symptoms and has felt the first movements. She travels often with her family and expects to travel again in the spring. She wants clear plans and prefers women clinicians
consultant_note.data_reviewed: The dating and nuchal translucency scan; cell-free DNA (low risk); blood group O RhD positive with a negative antibody screen; rubella immune; hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis C negative; urine culture no growth; hemoglobin electrophoresis normal; hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with ferritin 9 ng/mL at intake and 10.3 g/dL with ferritin 12 ng/mL today; hemoglobin A1c 5.4 percent; today's vital signs (blood pressure 106/64 mmHg, weight 59.8 kg)

assessment.assessment: A singleton pregnancy at an advanced maternal age with a low-risk aneuploidy screen. Age 35 or older raises the risks of preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, fetal growth restriction, and stillbirth; aspirin is correctly started

Thirteen previous births raise the risks of uterine atony and postpartum hemorrhage, malpresentation, and fast labor. Without a uterine scar, the risk of placenta accreta spectrum is low unless the placenta lies over the cervix
An interval under six months from birth to conception is linked to anemia, preterm birth, and a small baby
Iron deficiency anemia that has not responded to oral iron, which she cannot tolerate; thalassemia trait excluded. Anemia at delivery would leave her little reserve if she bleeds

recommendations: Intravenous iron now that she is in the second trimester: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg today and again in four weeks, with hemoglobin and ferritin before each dose and at 24 to 28 weeks; aim for a hemoglobin of at least 11 g/dL before delivery
Detailed anatomy scan at 20 to 22 weeks with placental location; if the placenta is low-lying or over the cervix, repeat at 32 weeks and assess for accreta; otherwise no MRI is needed

Continue aspirin 81 mg nightly until delivery; blood pressure and urine protein at every visit; glucose challenge at 24 to 28 weeks; visits every two weeks from 28 weeks and weekly from 36 weeks; a growth scan at 32 to 34 weeks; weekly fetal heart rate monitoring from 36 weeks can be offered
Birth in a hospital with a blood bank, 24-hour anesthesia, and an operating theatre; offer induction at 39 weeks, which also avoids an unplanned birth away from the hospital

Postpartum hemorrhage plan, written by 36 weeks: risk assessment on admission, type and screen, two large-bore lines, oxytocin 10 units at birth with controlled cord traction, quantitative blood loss, and, if hemorrhage occurs, tranexamic acid 1 g intravenously within 3 hours of birth with a second dose after 30 minutes if bleeding continues, alongside uterotonics, uterine massage, and the hemorrhage protocol; anesthesia consultation at 36 weeks

Travel is reasonable in the second trimester and early third trimester if she stays well: carry her records, keep her prenatal visits where she stays, walk and drink often on long journeys, and stay near the delivery hospital from 36 weeks
Discuss postpartum contraception and the interval before any future pregnancy in the third trimester, in her own terms; advise waiting at least 18 months, ideally 24, after this birth
